extraction.name: PASTIS (Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme Series)
extraction.description: PASTIS is the first large-scale, publicly available Satellite Image Time Series (SITS) dataset with both semantic and panoptic annotations. It is comprised of 2,433 sequences of multi-spectral images of shape 10×128×128, covering over 4,000 km² across four different regions of France. Each sequence contains between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019, for a total of over 2 billion annotated pixels. The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of the Sentinel-2 satellite after atmospheric correction and resampling at 10 meters per pixel. Each pixel is associated with a semantic label from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class, and each non-background pixel has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index. In total, 124,422 parcels are individualized, each with their bounding box, pixel-precise mask, and crop type.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot, Loic Landrieu (LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN)
extraction.citeAs: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot and Loic Landrieu. Panoptic Segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series with Convolutional Temporal Attention Networks. ICCV 2021.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were gathered from THEIA (value-added data processed by CNES for the Theia data cluster using Copernicus/Sentinel-2 data). The dataset spans four different Sentinel-2 tiles in different regions of the French metropolitan territory. All available acquisitions between September 2018 and November 2019 were stacked per patch. Acquisitions with more than 90% cloud cover were automatically filtered out by the Sentinel data provider THEIA. The annotations were taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS), as reported by the farmers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Passive Data Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover. Even after automatic filtering of predominantly cloudy acquisitions, some patches are still partially or completely obstructed by cloud cover. No further preprocessing or cloud detection was applied; raw data with cloud cover is retained in PASTIS. The temporal sampling is irregular: depending on location, patches are observed a different number of times and at different intervals, resulting in sequences of 33 to 61 acquisitions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentinel-2 satellite imagery obtained from the open-access Sentinel-2 platform via THEIA (https://scihub.copernicus.eu). The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of Sentinel-2 (all bands except atmospheric bands B01, B09, and B10), after atmospheric correction and resampling at 10 meters per pixel. Parcel annotations were taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS) produced by IGN, the French mapping agency.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: From approximately 24,000 available patches, 2,433 patches (about 10% of all available patches) were selected, favoring patches with rare crop types to decrease the otherwise extreme class imbalance. The FLPIS 73-class crop type breakdown was reduced to an 18-class nomenclature by selecting classes with at least 400 parcels and with samples in at least 2 of the 4 Sentinel-2 tiles. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of a patch are annotated with the void label. Bounding boxes are cropped along the patch extent. The 2,433 patches are split into 5 folds with a 1 km buffer between images to avoid cross-fold contamination, with each fold containing patches from all four Sentinel tiles and comparable class distributions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentinel-2 images underwent atmospheric correction and resampling to 10 meters per pixel by THEIA. Acquisitions with more than 90% cloud cover were automatically filtered out by the data provider. Each Sentinel-2 tile (100×100 km) was subdivided into square patches of size 1.28×1.28 km (128×128 pixels at 10 m/pixel). Only 10 non-atmospheric spectral bands were retained (B01, B09, B10 excluded). No further cloud detection or preprocessing was applied to the raw data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS), as reported by the farmers. Each pixel is annotated with a semantic label corresponding to either the parcel's crop type (from an 18-class nomenclature) or the background class. Each unique parcel pixel receives a corresponding instance label. Bounding boxes and pixel-precise masks are computed for each parcel. The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control at over 98%, with a relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS), produced by IGN, the French mapping agency
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes. Parcels belonging to classes not in the 18-class nomenclature are annotated with the void label. Parcels whose surface is more than 50% outside of the patch are also annotated with the void label. Predicted parcels overlapping with an IoU superior to 0.5 with a void parcel are ignored by the metric. The French Payment Agency estimates annotation accuracy via in situ control at over 98% with relative surface error under 0.3%.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each pixel receives one semantic label and, for non-background pixels, one instance label. Each parcel is annotated with a bounding box, a pixel-precise mask, and a crop type.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations were sourced from the French Land Parcel Identification System (FLPIS), as reported by farmers. No individual annotator demographics are provided.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available at https://github.com/VSainteuf/pastis-benchmark. A corrected evaluation implementation was released to fix a bug in the Recognition Quality (RQ) metric computation (see github.com/VSainteuf/utae-paps/issues/11). No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset supports remote monitoring of agricultural parcels, which is necessary for fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (approximately 50 billion euros per year in Europe and 22 billion in the US) and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected. More broadly, automated analysis of satellite image time series has implications for surveying urban development and deforestation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common crop classes. To mitigate this, patches with rare crop types were preferentially selected. The dataset covers only four regions of France, which may limit geographic diversity. Annotations reflect farmer self-reporting via the FLPIS, which may introduce reporting biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset covers only four regions of France, limiting geographic generalizability. Temporal sampling is irregular due to cloud cover filtering, resulting in sequences of varying length (33 to 61 acquisitions). Close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover. The dataset is limited to 18 crop types out of the 73 in the FLPIS. The dataset covers approximately 1% of the French Metropolitan territory. Performance drops significantly with reduced temporal sampling (e.g., -14.6 mIoU with only 8 available dates).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of panoptic segmentation models on satellite image time series. Semantic segmentation of crop types. Instance segmentation of agricultural parcels. Benchmarking of spatio-temporal encoding architectures for remote sensing. The official 5-fold cross-validation scheme is provided for benchmarking.
